Will the GNU hold?

By: Marion Edmunds | Commission

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
Carte Blanche asks whether the GNU will last?

Unique Selling Point:
South Africa will remain in suspense for months to come as the results of the 2024 national elections coalesce into some form of government. But already the failure of Gauteng Premier Panyaza Lesufi to build a representative GNU with the DA shows the faultlines which run underneath the surface of the newly constituted national power-sharing cabinet.

Summary:
We start the story about national politics with a provincial story - in Gauteng, where a defiant Premier, Panyaza Lesufi, takes the support of the Democratic Alliance to gain the provincial premier position, but then fails to deliver an executive power sharing agreement. It may be that it is in the interests of the DA to stay out Lesufi's cabinet, given the precariousness of government in Gauteng which is a service delivery catastrophe and a state capture nightmare. However this provincial political difficulty underscores the fragility of the national power sharing plan being led by Cyril Ramaphosa. We speak to some of the opposition party newbies in cabinet, and political commentators about the experience of this seismic shift of power and how illusive success will be for parties who are forced to work together to save the country's economy and people, but are still figuring out how to do so.

Press Release:


The Politics of Power
South Africa’s newly formed Government of National Unity is settling in, forging new alliances to build an accountable and effective government. But while political adversaries appear to be burying the hatchet at national level, old and new fault-lines threaten to scupper this fragile political marriage of convenience. In Gauteng, the failure to form a representative GNU is a symptom of deeper and darker political contests beneath the surface. Carte Blanche tests the waters with South Africa’s ministerial newbies, to establish the strength and nature of the glue in the GNU – and to ask, on whose shoulders will success ultimately rest?
Producer: Marion Edmunds | Presenter: Erin Bates
Watch the trailer

Script:


(VO1) SOUTH AFRICA’S RECENT ELECTIONS CHANGED EVERYTHING…
FOR THE FIRST TIME IN THREE DECADES OPPOSITION PARTIES HAVE A CHANCE TO PROVE THEMSELVES ON THE NATIONAL STAGE…

SIVIWE GWARUBE
Minister of Basic Education
We had viciously campaigned against one another. And we had to sit across the table and say, well, South Africans have decided.

(VO2) WITHIN WEEKS, A DIVERSE MIX OF POLITICAL LEADERS WERE HARNESSED INTO A TEN-PARTY POWER-SHARING AGREEMENT….

PIETER GROENEWALD
Minister of Correctional Services
We never asked for any position on cabinet. So that was quite a surprise.

(VO3) THE SEVENTH ADMINISTRATION IS CALLING ITSELF A GOVERNMENT OF NATIONAL UNITY
AND OUT OF THE UPHEAVAL OF THE LAST SIX WEEKS, THE G.N.U. IS SLOWLY REVEALING ITS SHAPE…

SONGEZO ZIBI
Chairperson of the Standing Committee on Public Accounts (SCOPA)
I don't think it has a character yet. It's still a bit messy.

(VO4)THIRTY YEARS AFTER SOUTH AFRICA’s TRANSITION TO DEMOCRACY, THE PEOPLE HAVE VOTED FOR A NEW DEAL.
NO ONE PARTY HAS EMERGED STRONG ENOUGH TO GOVERN ON IT’S OWN.
THIS MEANS THAT POLITICAL FOES HAVE BEEN FORCED TO WORK TOGETHER

ERIN PIECE TO CAM:

This Government of National Unity is made up of an alphabet soup of political parties, with three heavy hitters: The ANC, the DA and the IFP.

(VO5) UNDERSTANDING THE PRECISE NATURE OF THESE NEW RELATIONSHIPS IS THE WORK OF POLITICAL JOURNALISTS LIKE ASSOCIATE EDITOR OF THE DAILY MAVERICK, FERIAL HAFFAJEE.

FERIAL HAFFAJEE
Associate Editor, Daily Maverick
I was swatting up on a coalition - coalition's are very different animals because you have to sign agreements, which are pretty much cast in stone. ….Because we only had 12 days to come to some form of power sharing agreement, the GNU felt like the quickest way to get there, and something which had been tried and tested in our recent history.

(VO6) SOUTH AFRICA’S FIRST MULTI-PARTY G.N.U. IN 1994 WAS A WAY TO TRANSITION FROM APARTHEID TO A CONSTITUTIONAL DEMOCRACY.
BUT IT LASTED ONLY 18 MONTHS BEFORE FALLING APART..
SO HAS THIS ONE GOT STAYING POWER?

FERIAL HAFFAJEE
Associate Editor, Daily Maverick
It's a difficult crystal ball to, to read. This time, we have many more parties, who are part of the GNU so, keeping them all in the tent is going to be a work of quite nimble, political ballroom dancing.

(VO7) SIVIWE GWARUBE IS ONE OF THE ANC’S NEW DANCE PARTNERS.
ONCE CHIEF WHIP OF THE DEMOCRATIC ALLIANCE SHE HAS RETURNED TO PARLIAMENT AS THE COUNTRY’S YOUNGEST EVER MINISTER OF BASIC EDUCATION.
SHE’S STILL SPINNING AFTER THE TOUGH NEGOTIATIONS FOR POSITIONS IN CABINET.

SIVIWE GWARUBE
Minister of Basic Education
even when it got really, really difficult, I think there was a recognition of what was at stake. the future of the country hangs in these in these talks. And at some point, we're gonna have to check our egos at the door. They were long, they were gruelling. It was a long, 30 days of my life, post a very long election.

(VO8) THE COLLABORATION OF PARTIES WHO HAVE VEHEMENTLY DISAGREED WITH EACH OTHER ON ALMOST EVERY ASPECT OF GOVERNMENT MAKES THIS GNU A LANDMARK MOMENT. FOR SOME, IT’S BEEN A SHOCK.

ERIN: How hard a sell was the GNU deal to the DA party faithful, … you may consider that you have been co opted and silenced by the GNU?

SIVIWE GWARUBE
Minister of Basic Education
If we had sat this out and did not want to be part of the GNU, I'm not entirely sure that there would be much to save in 2029…. And what good is it then to intervene five years from now, when South Africa has really gone in the wrong direction? And how do you turn things around at that point?


(VO9) AS A FIRST TIME MEMBER OF PARLIAMENT, THIS FORMER NEWSPAPER EDITOR SONGEZO ZIBI IS THE NEW KID ON THE BLOCK.
HE IS REPRESENTING RISE MZANSI ONE OF THE YOUNGEST POLITICAL PARTIES.
ZIBI SIGNED UP FOR THE G.N.U., BUT STAYED OUT OF CABINET TO BUILD PARLIAMENT.

SONGEZO ZIBI
Chairperson of the Standing Committee on Public Accounts (SCOPA)
There's an opportunity for a fresh start. It's not possible to even pass money bills now without more than one political party cooperating, something South Africans have never seen, so that use of just the sheer power of your your number of seats has been neutralized. And so we're entering a new era that hopefully is of a mature democratic conversation where you have to convince people to agree with you

(VO10) ZIBI HAS BEEN ELECTED TO HEAD THE POWERFUL PARLIAMENTARY COMMITTEE WHICH FOLLOWS THE MONEY TRAIL AND INVESTIGATES SPENDING, THE STANDING COMMITTEE ON PUBLIC ACCOUNTS.
HE WANTS TO GIVE PARLIAMENT A SHOT IN THE ARM.

SONGEZO ZIBI
Chairperson of the Standing Committee on Public Accounts (SCOPA)
When people see that for the first time in a long time, Parliament is able to do its work by holding South Africans, their people in the executive to account then you might begin to see people returning to the polls, instead of staying at home.

ERIN BATES PIECE TO CAMERA:
A POWER SHARING GOVERNMENT IS A BALANCING ACT…
AND TO SURVIVETHIS GOVERNMENT OF NATIONAL UNITY WILL NEED TO MASTER THE ART OF COMPROMISE
OTHERWISE IT WILL ALL COME CRASHING DOWN.

(VO11) ALREADY THE FAILURE TO CREATE A PROVINCIAL GOVERNMENT OF NATIONAL UNITY IN GAUTENG SOURS THE MOOD AT NATIONAL LEVEL.

FERIAL HAFFAJEE
Associate Editor, Daily Maverick
The fact that the ANC would not yield significant enough positions or power in the government, and that's what led to the collapse of talks between the ANC and the DA, is because what you have here in the province is entrenched provincial capture. That's the way government is done in Gauteng. And I think what you saw was an effort to protect systems which have made people very wealthy, and which they didn't want to yield to the principles of power sharing.

(VO12)IN CONTRAST THE LEADER OF THE PATRIOTIC ALLIANCE, GAYTON MCKENZIE, HAS THROWN HIMSELF BOOTS AND ALL INTO THE NEW TEAM - AS THE MINISTER OF SPORT, ARTS AND CULTURE.

GM (in press conference): You know my personal opinion, the GNU is going to last, I am going to play the biggest role to make sure that I am one of the glue, one of the glue of the GNU of the Government of National Unity.

(VO13)BUT THE CULT OF PERSONALITY IS NOT ENOUGH TO HOLD THE CENTRE.
THE GNU’S FIRST BIG MEETING LAST WEEKEND LAID THE GROUND RULES FOR THE NEXT FIVE YEARS.
NEWLY MINTED MINISTERS LIKE INKATHA FREEDOM PARTY LEADER VELENKOSINI HLABISA CLAIM IT WENT BETTER THAN EXPECTED.

VELENKOSINI HLABISA
Minister of Cooperative Governance and Traditional Affairs (COGTA)
The mood was very good. …. That is why out of the two days, there was a smooth transition from different political parties into one government.

(VO14)HLABISA HAS DECADES OF SERVICE TO HIS COMMUNITY IN KWAZULU-NATAL AS AN EDUCATOR AND A MUNICIPAL COUNCILLOR.

VELENKOSINI HLABISA
Minister of Cooperative Governance and Traditional Affairs (COGTA)
I was living two lives, a political life, and a professional life. During the day, I was a teacher. After school, I became a politician. And I learned how to separate the two at work.

(VO15) THROWN TOGETHER IN A MELTING POT, THESE CABINET MINISTERS WITH THEIR CONTRASTING LIFE EXPERIENCES AND POLITICAL LANGUAGES MUST RUB TOGETHER IN TENSE MEETINGS BEHIND CLOSED DOORS.

SIVIWE GWARUBE
Minister of Basic Education
I think what really it is, is a marriage of pragmatism, because it had if we had all stuck to our ideological guns and ideological leanings, there was no way we could find each other. There was absolutely no way.

(VO16) PARTIES AS DIVERSE AS THE PAN AFRICANIST CONGRESS AND THE FREEDOM FRONT PLUS ARE NOW COMPARING NOTES. THE FREEDOM FRONT’S PIETER GROENEWALD SAYS HE EXPECTS THE CONSTITUTION WILL HELP TO GUIDE THEM AS ONE.

PIETER GROENEWALD,
Minister of Correctional Services
there is also a mechanism in the GNU, how to deal with those differences. In the end, they asking themselves whether there is sufficient consensus, that's a 60%. And part of that structure is that you go to a GNU Political Council, where you have all the role players, you debate the matter, you put your arguments forward. And there if 60% or more than agrees with whatever the outcome may be, then it becomes a decision.

(VO17) THE NEW MINISTER OF PRISONS IS STILL SETTLING IN. HE’S BEEN IN PARLIAMENT SINCE 1994, BUT NEVER IN POWER.
AND HE IS PROCESSING THIS DRAMATIC SHIFT IN HIS POLITICAL LIFE.

TIKTOK: Alfred Adriaan:
Oom Pieter lyk nie asof he kak vat nie, man.
Translation: Oom Pieter looks like he doesn’t take sh*t.

Jy kan mos sien.
Translation: You will see it.

Dis verby, Oom Pieter is op pad!
Translation: It’s over! Oom Pieter is coming!

PIETER GROENEWALD,
Minister of Correctional Services

Oom Pieter is op pad, ja,
Translation: Oom Pieter is coming, yes!

Maar ons moet vir mekaar se Oom Pieter kan dit nie alleen doen nie.
Translation: But we must add that Oom Pieter can’t do it on his own.

Hy kan hande vat saam met sy mense
Translation: He must be able to join hands with his people

en dan kan Oom Pieter 'n verskil maak
Translation: And then Oom Pieter can make a difference.

(VO18)GIVING THESE SMALLER PARTIES A SEAT AT THE TABLE MEANS THERE IS A CROWD IN CABINET – WITH 32 FULL MINISTERS, AND 43 DEPUTIES.
FERIAL HAFFAJEE
Associate Editor, Daily Maverick
Other than for China, say of the BRICS countries, it really is the biggest cabinet. Add in the broader executive, which is your deputy ministers and it's truly gargantuan. I think for so much government, we have to expect things of them. And they've got to find methods of making it work of finding, of finding mutuality and unity because that was the demand out of the elections.

(VO19)THIS WEEK, THE RED CARPET WAS ROLLED OUT TO USHER IN THE SEVENTH ADMINISTRATION, WITH IT’S WINNERS AND IT’S LOSERS IN ATTENDANCE.

ERIN PIECE TO CAM IN FRONT OF CITY HALL:
THIS CEREMONY IS A REALLY IMPORTANT STEP FOR THE GOVERNMENT OF NATIONAL UNITY.
IT SAYS, WE HAVE ARRIVED AND WE ARE READY TO GOVERN.

CYRIL RAMAPHOSA
President of South Africa
The coming together of all these parties that have decided to cooperate is quite a historic moment for our country. And we must make the Government of National Unity work. And function. And Succeed.

(VO20)THE MINISTER OF EDUCATION WAS IN THE AUDIENCE. GWARUBE KNOWS THAT THE REAL WORK IS ABOUT TO BEGIN.
SIVIWE GWARUBE
Minister of Basic Education
How you behave in this GNU will be reflected on your electoral outcomes in the future. And if you are somebody who's unprepared to work together to put the interests of South Africans first, the voters will punish you.



PROMO 1:
TEN PARTIES, 32 MINISTERS AND SCORES OF DEPUTIES - THIS CABINET IS TOP-HEAVY…
The future of 62 million people hangs in the balance.
AND THERE ARE GREAT EXPECTATIONS….
if we do not deliver, the voters will deal with us in next elections

PROMO 2:
CAN A PLUS SIZE CABINET MAKE THE RIGHT MOVES…
TO FIX A BROKEN NATION?
It's truly gargantuan. I think for so much government, we have to expect things of them.
There is now a whole lot of different political parties around the Cabinet table. ….and I think a little bit of healthy competition is going to help.

PROMO 3:
IN THE FACE OF AN ANGRY ELECTORATE…
People don't trust politicians at all. People don't trust political parties…
THE GNU GOES BIG AND BOLD.
You will need to understand that we are not in for your party, but we are in for the country..

SO HAS THIS ONE GOT STAYING POWER? FERIAL HAFFAJEE Associate Editor, Daily Maverick It's a difficult crystal ball to, to read. This time, we have many more parties, who are part of the GNU so, keeping them all in the tent is going to be a work of quite nimble, political ballroom dancing. (VO7) SIVIWE GWARUBE IS ONE OF THE ANC’S NEW DANCE PARTNERS. ONCE CHIEF WHIP OF THE DEMOCRATIC ALLIANCE SHE HAS RETURNED TO PARLIAMENT AS THE COUNTRY’S YOUNGEST EVER MINISTER OF BASIC EDUCATION. SHE’S STILL SPINNING AFTER THE TOUGH NEGOTIATIONS FOR POSITIONS IN CABINET. SIVIWE GWARUBE Minister of Basic Education even when it got really, really difficult, I think there was a recognition of what was at stake. the future of the country hangs in these in these talks. And at some point, we're gonna have to check our egos at the door. They were long, they were gruelling. It was a long, 30 days of my life, post a very long election. (VO8) THE COLLABORATION OF PARTIES WHO HAVE VEHEMENTLY DISAGREED WITH EACH OTHER ON ALMOST EVERY ASPECT OF GOVERNMENT MAKES THIS GNU A LANDMARK MOMENT. FOR SOME, IT’S BEEN A SHOCK. ERIN: How hard a sell was the GNU deal to the DA party faithful, … you may consider that you have been co opted and silenced by the GNU? SIVIWE GWARUBE Minister of Basic Education If we had sat this out and did not want to be part of the GNU, I'm not entirely sure that there would be much to save in 2029…. And what good is it then to intervene five years from now, when South Africa has really gone in the wrong direction? And how do you turn things around at that point? (VO9) AS A FIRST TIME MEMBER OF PARLIAMENT, THIS FORMER NEWSPAPER EDITOR SONGEZO ZIBI IS THE NEW KID ON THE BLOCK. HE IS REPRESENTING RISE MZANSI ONE OF THE YOUNGEST POLITICAL PARTIES. ZIBI SIGNED UP FOR THE G.N.U., BUT STAYED OUT OF CABINET TO BUILD PARLIAMENT. SONGEZO ZIBI Chairperson of the Standing Committee on Public Accounts (SCOPA) There's an opportunity for a fresh start. It's not possible to even pass money bills now without more than one political party cooperating, something South Africans have never seen, so that use of just the sheer power of your your number of seats has been neutralized. And so we're entering a new era that hopefully is of a mature democratic conversation where you have to convince people to agree with you (VO10) ZIBI HAS BEEN ELECTED TO HEAD THE POWERFUL PARLIAMENTARY COMMITTEE WHICH FOLLOWS THE MONEY TRAIL AND INVESTIGATES SPENDING, THE STANDING COMMITTEE ON PUBLIC ACCOUNTS. HE WANTS TO GIVE PARLIAMENT A SHOT IN THE ARM. SONGEZO ZIBI Chairperson of the Standing Committee on Public Accounts (SCOPA) When people see that for the first time in a long time, Parliament is able to do its work by holding South Africans, their people in the executive to account then you might begin to see people returning to the polls, instead of staying at home. ERIN BATES PIECE TO CAMERA: A POWER SHARING GOVERNMENT IS A BALANCING ACT… AND TO SURVIVETHIS GOVERNMENT OF NATIONAL UNITY WILL NEED TO MASTER THE ART OF COMPROMISE OTHERWISE IT WILL ALL COME CRASHING DOWN. (VO11) ALREADY THE FAILURE TO CREATE A PROVINCIAL GOVERNMENT OF NATIONAL UNITY IN GAUTENG SOURS THE MOOD AT NATIONAL LEVEL. FERIAL HAFFAJEE Associate Editor, Daily Maverick The fact that the ANC would not yield significant enough positions or power in the government, and that's what led to the collapse of talks between the ANC and the DA, is because what you have here in the province is entrenched provincial capture. That's the way government is done in Gauteng. And I think what you saw was an effort to protect systems which have made people very wealthy, and which they didn't want to yield to the principles of power sharing. (VO12)IN CONTRAST THE LEADER OF THE PATRIOTIC ALLIANCE, GAYTON MCKENZIE, HAS THROWN HIMSELF BOOTS AND ALL INTO THE NEW TEAM - AS THE MINISTER OF SPORT, ARTS AND CULTURE. GM (in press conference): You know my personal opinion, the GNU is going to last, I am going to play the biggest role to make sure that I am one of the glue, one of the glue of the GNU of the Government of National Unity. (VO13)BUT THE CULT OF PERSONALITY IS NOT ENOUGH TO HOLD THE CENTRE. THE GNU’S FIRST BIG MEETING LAST WEEKEND LAID THE GROUND RULES FOR THE NEXT FIVE YEARS. NEWLY MINTED MINISTERS LIKE INKATHA FREEDOM PARTY LEADER VELENKOSINI HLABISA CLAIM IT WENT BETTER THAN EXPECTED. VELENKOSINI HLABISA Minister of Cooperative Governance and Traditional Affairs (COGTA) The mood was very good. …. That is why out of the two days, there was a smooth transition from different political parties into one government. (VO14)HLABISA HAS DECADES OF SERVICE TO HIS COMMUNITY IN KWAZULU-NATAL AS AN EDUCATOR AND A MUNICIPAL COUNCILLOR. VELENKOSINI HLABISA Minister of Cooperative Governance and Traditional Affairs (COGTA) I was living two lives, a political life, and a professional life. During the day, I was a teacher. After school, I became a politician. And I learned how to separate the two at work. (VO15) THROWN TOGETHER IN A MELTING POT, THESE CABINET MINISTERS WITH THEIR CONTRASTING LIFE EXPERIENCES AND POLITICAL LANGUAGES MUST RUB TOGETHER IN TENSE MEETINGS BEHIND CLOSED DOORS. SIVIWE GWARUBE Minister of Basic Education I think what really it is, is a marriage of pragmatism, because it had if we had all stuck to our ideological guns and ideological leanings, there was no way we could find each other. There was absolutely no way. (VO16) PARTIES AS DIVERSE AS THE PAN AFRICANIST CONGRESS AND THE FREEDOM FRONT PLUS ARE NOW COMPARING NOTES. THE FREEDOM FRONT’S PIETER GROENEWALD SAYS HE EXPECTS THE CONSTITUTION WILL HELP TO GUIDE THEM AS ONE. PIETER GROENEWALD, Minister of Correctional Services there is also a mechanism in the GNU, how to deal with those differences. In the end, they asking themselves whether there is sufficient consensus, that's a 60%. And part of that structure is that you go to a GNU Political Council, where you have all the role players, you debate the matter, you put your arguments forward. And there if 60% or more than agrees with whatever the outcome may be, then it becomes a decision. (VO17) THE NEW MINISTER OF PRISONS IS STILL SETTLING IN. HE’S BEEN IN PARLIAMENT SINCE 1994, BUT NEVER IN POWER. AND HE IS PROCESSING THIS DRAMATIC SHIFT IN HIS POLITICAL LIFE. TIKTOK: Alfred Adriaan: Oom Pieter lyk nie asof he kak vat nie, man. Translation: Oom Pieter looks like he doesn’t take sh*t. Jy kan mos sien. Translation: You will see it. Dis verby, Oom Pieter is op pad! Translation: It’s over! Oom Pieter is coming! PIETER GROENEWALD, Minister of Correctional Services Oom Pieter is op pad, ja, Translation: Oom Pieter is coming, yes! Maar ons moet vir mekaar se Oom Pieter kan dit nie alleen doen nie. Translation: But we must add that Oom Pieter can’t do it on his own. Hy kan hande vat saam met sy mense Translation: He must be able to join hands with his people en dan kan Oom Pieter 'n verskil maak Translation: And then Oom Pieter can make a difference. (VO18)GIVING THESE SMALLER PARTIES A SEAT AT THE TABLE MEANS THERE IS A CROWD IN CABINET – WITH 32 FULL MINISTERS, AND 43 DEPUTIES. FERIAL HAFFAJEE Associate Editor, Daily Maverick Other than for China, say of the BRICS countries, it really is the biggest cabinet. Add in the broader executive, which is your deputy ministers and it's truly gargantuan. I think for so much government, we have to expect things of them. And they've got to find methods of making it work of finding, of finding mutuality and unity because that was the demand out of the elections. (VO19)THIS WEEK, THE RED CARPET WAS ROLLED OUT TO USHER IN THE SEVENTH ADMINISTRATION, WITH IT’S WINNERS AND IT’S LOSERS IN ATTENDANCE. ERIN PIECE TO CAM IN FRONT OF CITY HALL: THIS CEREMONY IS A REALLY IMPORTANT STEP FOR THE GOVERNMENT OF NATIONAL UNITY. IT SAYS, WE HAVE ARRIVED AND WE ARE READY TO GOVERN. CYRIL RAMAPHOSA President of South Africa The coming together of all these parties that have decided to cooperate is quite a historic moment for our country. And we must make the Government of National Unity work. And function. And Succeed. (VO20)THE MINISTER OF EDUCATION WAS IN THE AUDIENCE. GWARUBE KNOWS THAT THE REAL WORK IS ABOUT TO BEGIN. SIVIWE GWARUBE Minister of Basic Education How you behave in this GNU will be reflected on your electoral outcomes in the future. And if you are somebody who's unprepared to work together to put the interests of South Africans first, the voters will punish you. PROMO 1: TEN PARTIES, 32 MINISTERS AND SCORES OF DEPUTIES - THIS CABINET IS TOP-HEAVY… The future of 62 million people hangs in the balance. AND THERE ARE GREAT EXPECTATIONS…. if we do not deliver, the voters will deal with us in next elections PROMO 2: CAN A PLUS SIZE CABINET MAKE THE RIGHT MOVES… TO FIX A BROKEN NATION? It's truly gargantuan. I think for so much government, we have to expect things of them. There is now a whole lot of different political parties around the Cabinet table. ….and I think a little bit of healthy competition is going to help. PROMO 3: IN THE FACE OF AN ANGRY ELECTORATE… People don't trust politicians at all. People don't trust political parties… THE GNU GOES BIG AND BOLD. You will need to understand that we are not in for your party, but we are in for the country..

metadata.Unique Selling Point: South Africa will remain in suspense for months to come as the results of the 2024 national elections coalesce into some form of government. But already the failure of Gauteng Premier Panyaza Lesufi to build a representative GNU with the DA shows the faultlines which run underneath the surface of the newly constituted national power-sharing cabinet.
metadata.Summary: We start the story about national politics with a provincial story - in Gauteng, where a defiant Premier, Panyaza Lesufi, takes the support of the Democratic Alliance to gain the provincial premier position, but then fails to deliver an executive power sharing agreement. It may be that it is in the interests of the DA to stay out Lesufi's cabinet, given the precariousness of government in Gauteng which is a service delivery catastrophe and a state capture nightmare. However this provincial political difficulty underscores the fragility of the national power sharing plan being led by Cyril Ramaphosa. We speak to some of the opposition party newbies in cabinet, and political commentators about the experience of this seismic shift of power and how illusive success will be for parties who are forced to work together to save the country's economy and people, but are still figuring out how to do so.
